title: Optimize suggestions list query: remove N+1 lookups and cut p95 latency
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes: Suggestions API: reduced DB load and improved p95 latency for list retrieval; no API contract changes.
description: Context: After enabling the Suggestions view for a larger dogfood cohort, we saw suggestions list p95 increase and elevated DB CPU (see SRE alert thread + SUP-48293 notes on intermittent 'insufficient telemetry' when the API timed out). Root cause was an N+1 pattern in the suggestions list retrieval path: for each suggestion row we were issuing follow-up queries to fetch route metadata + latest computed estimate snapshot, plus a per-row RBAC scope check that also hit the DB. This PR removes those per-row queries by (1) fetching route/model display metadata in a single join, (2) selecting the latest estimate snapshot via a lateral join / window function rather than per-suggestion lookup, and (3) precomputing allowed project IDs once per request (RBAC) and applying it as a predicate in the main query. Results from staging load test (10 orgs, ~2k suggestions/org, list page size 50): p95 690ms -> 180ms; DB queries per request 112 -> 6; payload unchanged. No API contract changes. Notes: This keeps stable suggestion IDs intact and respects org/project scoping (audited). It also adds a query-level timeout + logs slow queries with tags optimize_suggestions_list. Rollout: safe to ship behind existing Suggestions flag; no migrations required.
commits: optimize(suggestions): replace per-row estimate fetch with latest-snapshot join
authz: cache RBAC project allow-list per request in suggestions handler
db: add composite index for suggestions_list(org_id, project_id, created_at desc)
observability: emit query_count + slow_query logs for suggestions list
tests: add regression test to assert bounded query count for list endpoint
implementation_notes: Key change is moving from: list_suggestions() -> for each suggestion: get_route(), get_latest_estimate(), check_permission() to a single query that returns all fields required for the table + drawer header. We use a window function to pick the newest estimate per (suggestion_id) within the org/project scope: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY suggestion_id ORDER BY computed_at DESC) = 1. RBAC is now resolved once, producing an allowed_project_ids array; the SQL uses project_id = ANY($allowed_project_ids). Added an index to support ordering + filtering: (org_id, project_id, updated_at DESC) plus include columns used by the select. Also added a conservative statement timeout for this query only (server-side), with structured logging when exceeded.
performance_results: Staging load test (k6, 50 rps, 10m, page_size=50): p50 120ms (was 260ms), p95 180ms (was 690ms), p99 310ms (was 1.2s). DB: CPU -35% during test; queries/request 6 (was ~112). No increase in error rate; one slow query event at p99 correlated with autovacuum; still under timeout.
risk_assessment: Low risk: no schema changes, no response shape changes, and the query is guarded by org/project predicates. Main risk is SQL correctness (latest snapshot selection) and RBAC filtering; covered via integration tests + added query budget regression to prevent reintroducing per-row selects.
test_plan: 1) Unit: run optimize-suggestions service tests. 2) Integration: list endpoint returns same suggestion IDs/ordering pre/post change for a fixed fixture dataset; verify latest estimate snapshot is selected. 3) Regression: assert query_count metric <= 8 for list endpoint at page_size=50. 4) Manual: open Console Suggestions list with filters/sorting; verify drawer opens without additional list refetch; validate RBAC-denied project does not leak suggestions.
review_conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can you confirm the window function still respects the same 'stale_as_of' behavior? Previously we fetched latest estimate and then applied staleness in app code. If we move selection into SQL, we should keep the same semantics.

Felix Schneider (author): Yep. The SQL picks the newest estimate row; the handler still computes stale_as_of from that row's computed_at and includes it unchanged. I added an integration test that sets computed_at older than the staleness threshold and checks stale_as_of is populated (same as before).
Dylan Brooks (review): Please add some guardrails to avoid silent regressions. A query budget test would be great, and also a metric to track queries per request for this endpoint.

Felix Schneider (author): Added services/optimize-suggestions/test/integration/list_suggestions_query_budget.test.ts and a request-scoped query counter emitted as optimize.suggestions.list.query_count. Also logs slow queries with org_id + route tags.
Aisha Bello (review): Any index changes? I’m worried about adding indexes late in beta without verifying impact. Also can we ensure statement timeout is scoped only to this query (not global)?

Felix Schneider (author): Added one composite index and verified it’s used in EXPLAIN on staging. Timeout is per-connection setting applied only around this query execution; it’s reset after. Included notes in the PR body and in code comments.
Allison Grant (review): Logging: please use standard structured fields (service, endpoint, org_id, duration_ms, rows) and don’t log raw SQL. Also add a dashboard link in the description if possible.

Felix Schneider (author): Updated logger fields to match observability standards; no SQL text logged. Added a note referencing the Suggestions API dashboard panel 'DB queries/request' (Grafana: Optimize Suggestions Service).
Chloe Martin (approval): Looks good. The integration tests cover the tricky parts and the query budget test should prevent drift.
Dylan Brooks (approval): Approved. Thanks for pushing this quickly—should help with the p95 regression alert.
